svg.title: TOPAK H10 — User documentation is a derived layer: a document set for every role, a projection rebuilt from every revision, and a reader over the public API alone
svg.desc: Three records drafted on one day answer one request of the custodian. ADR-0071 makes user documentation a derived layer that decides nothing: twenty-one readers in three positions, forty-three documents (the diagram's count) across Build, Run, governance, external, every reader and the overlay, each unit read at three levels (MI, SI, DI) where a level may leave out and never add, every DI statement bound by digest to the clause, module, policy and code it describes, and a release cut under seven mechanical gates. ADR-0072 serves it as a projection of the corpus at a commit that can be dropped and rebuilt to the same digests: every revision immutable and addressed by SHA-256, every checkpoint and release a view equal to latest, one table with a composite key behind the DynamoDB interface, GraphQL and REST generated from one model and read-only. ADR-0073 is the reference reader, React with Material UI, a client of that API and nothing more, with reflow, two colour schemes, a reading mode that never hides a mark, assistive access, and WCAG 2.2 AA as a dated audit a person signs. All three are Proposed and nothing in them is modelled, checked or built: no unit is written, no gate is a program, no service, store, API or reader exists, and no dependent entry is drafted.
svg.text: TOPAK · H10

cut under seven mechanical gates. ADR-0072 serves it as a projection of the corpus at a commit that can be dropped and rebuilt to the same digests: every revision immutable and addressed by SHA-256, every checkpoint and release a view equal to latest, one table with a composite key behind the DynamoDB interface, GraphQL and REST generated from one model and read-only. ADR-0073 is the reference reader, React with Material UI, a client of that API and nothing more, with

reflow, two colour schemes, a reading mode that never hides a mark, assistive access, and WCAG 2.2 AA as a dated audit a person signs. All three are Proposed and nothing in them is modelled, checked or built: no unit is written, no gate is a program, no service, store, API or reader exists, and no dependent entry is drafted.

text.tspan: Proposed · C2 · drafted 2026.11.16, R1 the same day
Proposed · C2 on the drafter's reading · 2026.11.16, R1
Proposed · no marker on the drafter's reading · 2026.11.16, R1
the service: ingest, store, API, search
rests on ADR-0057, ADR-0069, ADR-0074 to ADR-0076

svg.text: Proposed means nothing here is in force. The custodian's request of 2026.11.16, one message and not a discussion, settled twelve things across ADR-0071 to ADR-0076, numbered ⟨K1⟩ to ⟨K12⟩ once for the six records; these three use ⟨K1⟩ to ⟨K10⟩. Every other choice is the drafter's, marked *(drafter's choice)*, *(drafter's recommendation)* or *(drafter's reading)* in the records, and each ratification condition ends with the custodian's reading of them. Each record was renumbered up by one on 2026.11.16 (R1) because ADR-0070

was taken by a record in flight on another branch; no decision text changed. G12 counts the three among its 27 Proposed records and lists them at item 116: "Nothing built, no module, no dependent entry drafted." One author, one day, no reader other than the drafter.

text.tspan: The three records as one picture: the corpus is the source, the service projects it, the reader shows it, the people read it (ADR-0072 §1, §9; ADR-0071 §2, §3; ADR-0073 §1)
The corpus at a commit: the sources
The unit files, the records, modules and policies they bind to, and

svg.text: the manifests (ADR-0072 §1 P-1). Units live in one tree, one file to a
unit; the tree's name and the file's form are not fixed (ADR-0071 §9).
No unit is written (ADR-0071 Status note).
The archive of record keeps them (ADR-0074 §2, class C;
Proposed). The service is a system of record for nothing, in ADR-0005
§1's sense (P-1).
Where a unit and a record disagree, the record wins, and the state
of record is the latest checkpoint (ADR-0071 §1 D-1).
DG-1 to DG-7 run first, and nothing is written for a unit that fails one
(ADR-0072 §9 I-4; ADR-0071 §8). Each gate is a program named by
digest, mechanical as ADR-0007 requires.
Ingest is the only way in, and it starts on a digest: given a commit it
resolves a tree and records its digests; a cut is given the checkpoint's
or release's manifest and refuses a tree that does not verify (I-1, I-2).
Run twice on one commit it writes nothing the second time (I-3). A
carrier's merge moves latest and is not a cut (I-5).
Not built: no gate is a program (ADR-0071 §12).

text.tspan: The store: revisions by digest, views as manifests, one table

svg.text: A revision is the SHA-256 of a unit's canonical bytes, written once (ADR-0072 §2
L-1, L-2); reachable by digest, by number from 1 with no gaps, and by time (L-3);
nothing ages out (L-5).
A view is a named manifest: latest moves; G12 and DOC-<date> are cut once and
never change; every operation takes a view and none is defined for latest alone (§4

text.tspan: One table, a composite key, two global and one local index; no operation scans;

svg.text: an overwrite fails at the store (§5; Annex A). The reference's engine is ExtendDB on
PostgreSQL (§6, drafter's recommendation): nothing in this corpus has run it.

text.tspan: The GraphQL schema and the OpenAPI description are generated

svg.text: from one model file by a pinned tool, neither edited by hand (§7 A-1);
equal, under a parity test (A-2); read-only: no mutation, no method but
GET and HEAD (A-3).
Every response names its view and its revision digests (A-4, V-6);
a cut view's response is immutable and cached without limit. Seven
operations (A-5, drawn below). Search is a second projection, built per
view (A-8).
Not built: there is no service, no store and no API (Status note).

text.tspan: The reference reader, and any other client
React with Material UI, a client of the public API and nothing more

svg.text: (ADR-0073 §1 R-1, §2): no credential a third party's reader could not
hold, no content of its own (R-2), nothing said of its own but navigation,
labels and its accessibility statement (R-3), one code path for every view
None is privileged: a page, an application, a terminal, a program, an
embeddable element (ADR-0072 §8 U-1, U-5). Content comes as a
typed tree, marks and bindings as data (U-2, U-4).
No reader exists (ADR-0073 Status note). The corpus is read today as
Markdown that a carrier renders.

text.tspan: The people: twenty-one readers, three positions

svg.text: Inside the proofs, holding a seat: AU-1 to AU-5, the operator, a
grant seat, an author in Build, the person seated in an
emergency, the overlay seats (ADR-0071 §2).
At the gate, or a trust root: AU-6 to AU-12, the anchor
key-holder, the break-glass and erasure rosters, the custodian,
pipeline keys, trust roots outside the mechanism, the responder.
Outside the deployment: AU-13 to AU-21, reviewer, audit
authority, adopter, agent developer, supplier, acquirer, a person
acted for, the reporter, a vehicle builder.
Forty-three documents for them (the diagram's count of §3's
rows: Build 9, Run 8, governance 9, external 9, every reader 7,
the overlay 1). Unwritten, except two drafts (Ex-1, Ex-2) and one
file (Ex-8) (S-2).
①
②
③
④
⑤
Node: a record's clause; a module and a named property; a proof
module or a Lean file; a floor stage or a policy; a Rego rule; a crate or
a function; a schema; a results file; a trusted-base row; a degeneracy;
a glossary entry; a checkpoint item.
Pin: the node's digest when the unit was read against it, a clause's
once ADR-0057 §7's clause pins exist and the file's until then. Relation
: decides, states, enforces, implements, evidences, assumes, defines.
Reader: who read the unit against the node.
A binding is a pinned citation and not an edge (B-5; ADR-0057 §3):
a unit discharges nothing and moves no theorem's grade.
A binding whose pin no longer matches its node is stale, and so is
the unit (ST-1). It is served and says so, naming the node that moved
(ST-2). Only a reading clears it; no program re-pins (ST-3). A cut
view keeps the pins it was cut with (ST-4; ADR-0072 §4 V-2).
A fifth manifest kind, documentation, over the unit files at a commit,
cut with each checkpoint and whenever the custodian cuts one
between *(drafter's choice)*; ADR-0072 §4 makes a view of it.
What no gate checks: that a unit says what its clause says. DG-2
finds a binding and cannot read it. So each unit names who read it
against its bindings (RL-1); during genesis a release promotes nothing
and is cut by the custodian (RL-2); after bootstrap, open (RL-3).
Not cut; manifests/README.md lists four kinds (§12).

text.tspan: A unit's life, and the three views (ADR-0072 §3, §4)

svg.text: drafted, released, superseded, withdrawn: computed from revisions and views,
never stored on the immutable revision (LC-1). Withdrawal is a revision, not a removal
(LC-2). Disposal is not a state: a unit holds no cognitive payload (LC-4; §10 H-1).
latest follows the newest ingest of the default branch and is the only view that
changes; G12 is cut with each Genesis Checkpoint against its manifest; DOC-<date>
with each documentation release. Cut views are written once and never removed
Rebuild ⑥: dropping the store and ingesting again yields the same digests, checked
by comparing them (P-2; ADR-0069 §10.2's results rule).
It never writes (A-3): content enters by ingest and by no request. A
version only grows (A-6): a field is added or deprecated with a date,
never repurposed. A request cannot exhaust it by its shape (A-7):
paged by cursor, bounded in depth and cost; this protects availability
and nothing else.
Who may read is the deployment's rule (§8 U-6): the archetype's
units are public under LICENSE-DOCS; a deployment's own may be
restricted, which hides a unit and changes none.

text.tspan: What the reader must show (ADR-0073 §3 to §7)

svg.text: One document that reflows from 320 CSS pixels and at 400% zoom
(RD-1). Two schemes, the first visit following the device, both at the
same contrast (LD-1, LD-2). Reading mode is the page as the server
sends it, needing no script, and it may hide navigation and never a mark
or a binding (RM-1, RM-4; ADR-0029 §3). Assistive access as nine
requirements AA-1 to AA-9.
Conformance is WCAG 2.2 Level AA as a dated audit: a computed
part that refuses and never admits, and an examined part by a person
who did not write the reader; a release says *checked* or *claimed*
(WC-1 to WC-3). No report, no auditor (§9).

text.tspan: Three levels, and the record wins (ADR-0071 §4, §1,

svg.text: MI: what is this, and what may I do and not do? SI: how does it
work, and how do I do it? DI: exactly what, and on whose
authority? A level may leave out, and it never adds (LV-2). A
limit travels with the guarantee it limits (LV-3): a reader who
stops at MI has read less, not something more favourable.
The documentation decides nothing ⑦. A wrong document
subtracts, or moves a person within a bound a theorem already
assumes: an operator still signs one of six admitted actions; the
anchor is already a havoc issuer (§11). No degeneracy, no
trusted-base row. It does not make its readers right: A5 stays
an assumption of use.

text.tspan: The sources: the corpus at a commit (ADR-0072 §1 P-1)
The service: a projection that can be rebuilt, and a system of record for nothing (ADR-0072)

svg.text: ⑥
⑦
The arrows, each with its clause
The corpus at one commit, read by ingest: a commit resolved to a tree and its digests; for a cut, the checkpoint's or the release's manifest, and a tree that does not verify against it is refused

Revisions, bindings and, for latest, a manifest, written once: a revision and a cut view's entries are put with a condition that the key does not exist, and a second, different write of a cut view is refused
Reads that are key conditions: every operation is a GetItem or a Query on the table or one index, and no operation scans
ADR-0072 §5 S-2; Annex A
GET and HEAD, and GraphQL without a mutation, with cross-origin reads allowed for the public units; the reader calls this and nothing else
A unit at MI, SI or DI with its marks and bindings, in whichever view the address names, the view named on the page, every mark a word
Rebuild: the store is dropped and ingested again from the corpus, and the rebuild is checked by comparing digests and not by trust in the rebuild

The record wins, and the documentation decides nothing: the service admits no action, counts no vote and issues nothing; the reader states nothing of its own; where a unit and a record disagree, the record wins and the disagreement is a
finding against the unit. Dashed: this path carries no authority
the corpus: records and what they cite
Proposed: the service and the reader, not built
the people who read
a rebuild, checked by digest
no authority: the record wins
what does not exist

text.tspan: ADR-0071 · User documentation is a derived layer with a document set for every role (Context; §1)
Context: written for the people who judge it, not yet for the people who would act under it

svg.text: A Reviewer's Guide and an Adopter's Guide, both drafts; a Theory of Operation, a glossary and an architecture description whose stakeholder table names eight readers. No

text.tspan: document for an operator, a key-holder, a grant seat, a break-glass roster or the person seated by one, an erasure roster, or an auditor.

svg.text: ToO assumption A5: "A trained, authorized human is present". No record says what the training is, and nothing exists to train from.

text.tspan: Three things in the corpus shape the answer

svg.text: A document that restates a guarantee can misstate it. "Where the narrative and the current checkpoint disagree, the checkpoint wins" (narrative/README.md); "Where a
diagram and a record disagree, the record wins" (diagrams/README.md). The Adopter's Guide: "Every must cites the record clause it comes from", "Every should is advice the
records do not contain".
A summary is where a caveat is lost. Progressive disclosure, done carelessly, discloses the guarantee first and the limit three clicks later.
Some readers are inside the proofs and some are not. "A principal is anything evictable by an authority other than itself. Whatever is not is at the gate." An operator is
bounded by the admit path; a key-holder at archetype custody only by the rules floor (§11).
D-1. A unit states what records, modules, policies and code already state, for a named reader. Where a unit and a record disagree, the record wins; the disagreement is a
finding against the unit, "whichever layer is right".
D-2. Documentation ranks last. In the Reviewer's Guide's order (state of record, decisions, narrative, evidence, derived) it sits with the derived layer and below the narrative,
which it may cite and never overrides.
D-3. Three kinds of sentence, and each says which it is: a must (*cannot*, *never*) restates a clause and is bound to it (§5); a should is advice the records do not contain,
marked *advice*, and binds nobody; where the corpus supplies nothing and a deployment has to, the unit says "the deployment writes this" and names the open item.
D-4. A unit does not supply what no record decides. It says that no record decides it and cites the open obligation; it does not invent the procedure. §3's last column lists
where this bites.
D-5. A unit carries the status of what it describes (§5 B-6), at every level it speaks at.
A-1. The list is every person or organization the corpus names as acting on a deployment or judging it; a role a record names that has no row is a finding against this record.
A-2. A record that adds a role owes a row, as a record that adds a term owes the narrative its definition.
A-3. One person may be several readers: "A person who operates and also votes holds two seats and is two principals" (ADR-0037), and the documents follow the seats.
A-4. The assistant is not a reader of user documentation. Its documents are the skills; a model at a seat learns its tools from the mechanism (ADR-0048), never from a unit.

text.tspan: §2 · "principals at the gate" read as two groups (drafter's reading)

svg.text: The corpus defines each against the other, so no reader is both at once. The table adds a third group the request's "etc." covers: readers outside the deployment.
S-1. Every reader of §2 appears in at least one row, and every row names at least one reader; DG-6 computes both.
S-2. The set is a list of what is owed, not of what exists. Two rows have a draft today (Ex-1, Ex-2) and one has a file (Ex-8). The rest are unwritten.
S-3. A document whose records are all Proposed may be written and is marked (§5 B-6): it describes a design not in force, and says so at its head.
S-4. Operators have one document in each domain (Bd-1, Rn-1), because the seat is "declared in the issued rules with a domain" (ADR-0050 §1). The corpus names no "Build
operator" role, and this record adds none.

text.tspan: The request's domains and the drafter's two more (§3)

svg.text: Build, Run, external and governance are the request's ⟨K2⟩. Its "etc." is read as what every reader needs (Cx) and the Proposed command-chain overlay (Ov) *(drafter's
reading)*.

§4 · Three levels of disclosure ⟨K3⟩ (the letters are the custodian's; *main*, *supporting*, *detailed* is the drafter's reading; the pattern is C4's, taken as follows, drafter's choice)
What is this, and what may I do and not do?
The subject in one screen: what the reader's role is here, what the system guarantees them, what it does not, and what they must never do
1, context: the reader and what they touch
How does it work, and how do I do it?
The parts the subject passes through and the procedure: steps, preconditions, what is recorded, what cannot be undone
2 and 3, containers and components; a sequence where order matters
Exactly what, and on whose authority?
Every action, field, rule, bound and error, each bound to its sources (§5)
4, code: the clause, the property, the policy rule, the function. A table, not a drawing
LV-1. A unit has all three, and neither MI nor DI is empty.
LV-2. A level may leave out, and it never adds. Every statement at MI is made at SI, and every one at SI is made at DI, where it is bound. MI is a selection from DI and has
no claim of its own.
LV-3. A limit travels with the guarantee it limits: the same level states its status mark, what it assumes, and the residual a record declares. A reader who stops at MI has
read less, not something more favourable.
LV-4. Each level answers its own question without the next. MI is not a teaser for SI.
LV-5. A diagram depicts and decides nothing; each carries a short text alternative and a long description (ADR-0072 §8 U-3).
LV-6. MI fits one screen *(advice)*: about 150 words and one diagram.
B-1. At DI every statement is bound: the clause that *decides* it, and beside it what *states* it in a model, *enforces* it in policy, *implements* it and *evidences* it. Where
one does not exist, the unit says so: "no module states this", "not built". An absence is written and never left blank (ADR-0057 §2's "none yet", "stated as a claim").
B-2. At SI every must, cannot and never is bound to its clause, and every control step names the action and the clause that gives its preconditions.
B-3. At MI a binding is owed wherever MI states a guarantee or a limit, and each unit's MI binds at least the record that defines its subject.
B-4. A should is bound to nothing and says *advice*.
B-5. A binding is a pinned citation and not an edge: it discharges nothing, contributes no premise and moves no theorem's grade; it uses the specification graph's node ids
where the graph has the node, so the graph's checker can report stale bindings beside stale edges (ADR-0057 §3, §8). The graph today has no node for a narrative file or a
guide.
B-6. Every bound record's status is shown in the corpus's own words, at each level (table at right). Evidence is named only of what ran: proved (TLAPS), checked (TLC, with the
constants), proved in Lean, tested, built at the reference, not built.
B-7. A bound overlay record is marked as an overlay.

text.tspan: §5's first table, whole: the four parts of a binding

svg.text: Node: one of a record's clause (by record, section and amendment tags); a module and a named property; a proof module or a Lean file; a floor stage or a policy in it; a Rego
policy or rule; a crate or a function; a format's schema; a results file; a trusted-base row; a degeneracy; a glossary entry; a checkpoint item.
Pin: the digest of the node's content when the unit was read against it: a clause's digest once ADR-0057 §7's clause pins exist, and the file's until then.
Relation: *decides* (a record clause), *states* (a model), *enforces* (a policy), *implements* (code), *evidences* (a result), *assumes* (a row), *defines* (a glossary entry).
Reader: who read the unit against the node, and whether that person drafted the unit.

§6 · A unit, whole, with U-1 to U-3; §7 · Staleness; §8 · A release, and what its gates can and cannot check
Stable, and never reused. The document's id and a short name: Rn-1/revoke
*concept*, *task*, *reference* or *troubleshooting* *(drafter's choice)*
From §2 and §3
§5, each attached to the statement it supports
Declared, with any passage in another marked

U-1. A task's steps are numbered, and each control action says four things: what it needs (a lease, a peer), what the log records of it, whether it adds or denies, and whether it can be undone. For the six operator actions these are
ADR-0050 §4's columns, bound and not paraphrased.
U-2. A unit is the smallest thing revised, released and withdrawn (ADR-0072 §2, §3).
U-3. A unit holds no example taken from a round (ADR-0072 §10 H-1).
ST-1. A binding whose pin no longer matches its node is stale, and so is the unit, at each level the binding supports.
ST-2. A stale unit is served and says it is stale, naming the node that moved. Not hidden, because the procedure it holds may be the only one; not shown as current.

ST-3. Only a reading clears it. A person reads the changed node, brings the unit into line or records why it already is, and re-pins. No program re-pins. This is the review ADR-0057 §3 asks of a stale edge.
ST-4. A cut view keeps the pins it was cut with (ADR-0072 §4 V-2). Staleness is a fact about latest, and about a past view only as a note beside it.
Every binding's node exists at the commit, and the gate has computed which pins match. A release may contain a stale unit only marked as one
Every DI statement row has a *decides* binding, and each of its other relations has a binding or a written absence. Every SI sentence with must, cannot or never has a binding
Each bound record's status, read from its Status and Pending lines at the commit, appears at each level that binds it
Every unit has MI, SI and DI, and MI and DI are not empty
Every figure has both descriptions, every table its headers, every unit its language
The coverage report exists: for each reader of §2 and each document of §3, its units, or the word *unwritten*. The gate passes once the report is written, as ADR-0069 §3a's IG-7 does
No unit includes a file from outside the documentation tree

text.tspan: §8 · The release, and RL-1 to RL-3

svg.text: A documentation release is a manifest over the unit files at a commit, cut with each checkpoint and whenever the custodian cuts one between *(drafter's choice: the narrative's rhythm)*. A fifth kind, documentation, beside the four manifests/README.md lists. The gates are programs named by digest
(ADR-0069 §6 G-1), each mechanical (ADR-0007). Not built, not cut.
What no gate checks: that a unit says what its clause says. Whether MI left out a limit, whether a step restates a precondition rightly, and whether a should is really advice are a person's to judge.
RL-1. Each unit names who read it against its bindings; a unit read only by its drafter says so, in ADR-0029 A2's words.
RL-2. During genesis a release promotes nothing (ADR-0069 §10.3); it is cut by the custodian.

RL-3. After bootstrap, whether a release is promoted is open *(drafter's recommendation: not a class under ADR-0024 §1, because the mechanism loads none of it; a unit of Rn-3, Rn-8, Gv-2, Gv-3 or Gv-6 is read before release by a member of the roster or key set it instructs)*.
§9 · What exists today; §10 · A deployment's documentation; §11 · Degeneracy and the trusted base; §12 · Ratification condition, item by item

text.tspan: §9 · What exists today (drafter's choice throughout). No file is moved or changed by this record

svg.text: The two guides become Ex-1 and Ex-2 when they are next rewritten, as units; until then they stand as drafts that manifests/EXCLUDE leaves unmeasured.
The Theory of Operation and the glossary stay the narrative; units bind to them (Cx-1, Cx-2) and do not replace them. The architecture description stays an index.
The READMEs' instructions for running things are the source of Cx-5.
Units live in one tree, one file to a unit. The tree's name and the unit file's form are not fixed here (Open obligations).
An overlay on these: it keeps, replaces, adds or omits by unit id (ADR-0072 §10 H-3). Where §3's last column says *the deployment writes this*, the overlay is where it is
written. A replacement carries its own reader (RL-1) and inherits no reading from the archetype's.

text.tspan: §11 · No degeneracy is declared, and no row is added

svg.text: A reader inside the proofs can be misled only as far as the mechanism admits. An operator who follows a wrong step still signs one of six actions, each admitted or
refused on the lease, the peer and the floor (ADR-0050 §4). A grant seat who misreads casts a vote the tally counts as any other. The theorems take these principals as
Mediated and attributable, not as correct.
A reader at the gate is already assumed to do anything the rules floor allows. The anchor is "a havoc issuer" (ADR-0025's title), and a document cannot widen what havoc
reaches.
So a wrong document subtracts, or moves a person within a bound a theorem already assumes. By ADR-0045 §2's test it is not a trust root.
What this does not make harmless: a revocation that should have been made, an emergency seating that should not have been, an issuance the floor permits and nobody
wanted. Inside the bounds, and still harms. A5 stays an assumption of use; this record gives it something to point at and does not discharge it.
The readers of §2 are checked against the corpus by someone who is not the drafter, and every role a record names has a

text.tspan: Annex A · dependent entries this record would owe

svg.text: 1. manifests/README.md. A fifth kind, documentation, and its row. Not a record; changed with the first cut. Not drafted.
2. ADR-0057 §1 (Proposed). R-revision (dependent on ADR-0071, Proposed), only if the custodian wants documentation named as a layer. B-5 does not need it. Not drafted.
3. The Adopter's Guide and the Reviewer's Guide. No entry. They are not records, and §9 leaves them as they are.
4. ADR-0029 §3. No entry. B-6 restates its two phrases and changes neither.
ADR-0072 and ADR-0073 list no dependent entry: each carries a debt against nothing and closes nothing.

text.tspan: ADR-0072 · The documentation service is a projection that can be rebuilt (Context; §1, §2, §3, §4)
Proposed · C2 on the drafter's reading · drafted 2026.11.16, R1

svg.text: The corpus already keeps every revision of everything, and offers a reader one of them. A record changes only by a typed History row; a checkpoint is "one cut, never
revised"; a derived document "is never revised, a new one is written"; a manifest is verified "against the tree it measured, not against today's". What a reader is given is the
head of a branch on a carrier; to read the ToO at G9 one runs git diff between two tags.
"Equal to the latest" is the hard word ⟨K10⟩. A system that keeps old versions as downloads beside a live site has kept them and has not made them equal.
A store of documentation must not become a second record. ADR-0005 §1 makes the archive the system of record. A store that held the only copy of a revision would be a
record nobody decided to keep.

text.tspan: §1 · The service is a projection, and it can be rebuilt

svg.text: P-1. The store holds nothing that is not derived from the corpus at a commit, by a pinned program. The unit files, the records, modules and policies they bind to, and the
manifests are the sources; the archive of record keeps them (ADR-0074 §2, class C; Proposed). Not a system of record for anything.
P-2. Dropping the store and ingesting again yields the same digests, checked by comparing digests and not by trust in the rebuild (ADR-0069 §10.2's results rule,
applied to a store).
P-3. The service decides nothing. It admits no action, counts no vote and issues nothing. Where a unit and a record disagree, the record wins (ADR-0071 §1).

text.tspan: §2 · A revision is immutable and is addressed by its digest ⟨K10⟩

svg.text: L-1. A unit's revision is the SHA-256 of its canonical bytes: three levels, bindings and metadata in a fixed serialization. The digest identifies; a number, a date and a commit
locate (ADR-0069 §9 C-5).
L-2. A revision is written once. No operation edits or deletes one. A correction is a new revision.
L-3. Every revision of every unit is reachable three ways: by digest; by unit and revision number, from 1 with no gaps; by unit and a time, which returns the revision in force
then.
L-4. Two revisions can be compared, level by level and binding by binding, through the API (§7).
L-5. Nothing ages out: no expiry, no tiering a reader cannot reach, no limit on revisions kept. How long the sources are kept is ADR-0075's schedule, class C.
LC-1. The states are computed from revisions and views, not stored on the immutable revision. A revision released at G12 and superseded since is both, and each view shows
it as that view saw it.
LC-2. Withdrawal is a revision, not a removal. An old link reaches the old text under a line saying it was withdrawn, when, and by which revision.
LC-3. Staleness is separate from state (ADR-0071 §7); a stale revision may be drafted, released or superseded as well.
LC-4. Disposal is not a state. No cognitive payload (§10 H-1), so no erasure under ADR-0006 reaches a unit, and the service has no path that destroys a revision.
V-1. Every operation takes a view, and none is defined for latest alone. The contract tests run once against latest and once against a cut view, and a difference fails
them.
V-2. A cut view answers from the corpus as it stood: a binding in G12 pins the digest its node had at that cut, and the service shows that text, saying separately whether the
node has changed since. It never rewrites a cut view to agree with today.
V-3. A cut view is written once, under its manifest's digest; a second write that differs is refused.
V-4. Views are never removed. A view of a checkpoint later known to be wrong stays, carrying that statement as a notice (checkpoints/README.md's own rule).
V-5. Two views compare by set difference on digests: added, removed, changed (ADR-0069 §3 I-5).
V-6. latest always says what it resolved to, so a reader can cite what they read and reach it again.
V-7. Checkpoints cut before the service exists get backfilled views *(drafter's choice)*: the narrative, the two guides and the READMEs as each manifest measured them,
one level, no bindings, marked backfilled; G1 and G2 as far as manifests/index.tsv says they verify.
§3 · A unit has a life, whole ⟨K10⟩
Ingested from a commit and in no cut view. Shown in latest with the word *draft*
Ingest (§9)
Named by the manifest of a checkpoint view or a release view
The cut (§4)
A later revision of the same unit exists
The later revision's ingest. The earlier one is unchanged
The unit's newest revision says the unit is withdrawn, why, and what replaces it
A withdrawing revision. Earlier revisions and the views naming them are unchanged
§4 · A view is a manifest, whole ⟨K10⟩: for each unit one revision digest, with the corpus commit and the corpus manifest it was cut against
Never cut. It follows the newest ingest of the default branch
Yes. It is the only view that does
G12, and so on
With each Genesis Checkpoint, against the checkpoint's own manifest
Never
DOC-<date>, or a promoted release's digest
With each documentation release (ADR-0071 §8); after bootstrap, with each publication under ADR-0069 §8
Never
§5 · The store ⟨K5⟩; §6 · The reference's engine; §7 · One model, two generated interfaces ⟨K6⟩; §8 · Any reader may integrate ⟨K7⟩

text.tspan: §5 · One table with a composite primary key and secondary indexes, reached only through the DynamoDB data model and API

svg.text: S-1. One table. Every item has a partition key and a sort key, and its type is read from the two together; items read together share a partition.
S-2. Every access pattern is a key condition: a GetItem or a Query with a partition key and a range of the sort key. No operation scans. A pattern that cannot be listed in
Annex A is not offered.
S-3. Secondary indexes carry the other readings: two global, one local (Annex A).
S-4. Immutability is a conditional write: put with a condition that the key does not exist; an overwrite fails at the store, not in the service's code.
S-5. A view is cut in one transaction, or under a marker: the head item is written last, and a view without its head is not served.
S-6. The engine is open source: an OSI-approved licence, the reference's build pinned by digest.

text.tspan: §6 · ExtendDB on PostgreSQL, and the interface is what is fixed (drafter's recommendation)

svg.text: What supports it: it implements §5's interface with composite keys, both index kinds, conditional writes and transactions, as its README and differences document state;
Apache-2.0 on PostgreSQL's licence; written in Rust, as the reference mechanism is.
What does not: it is new. AWS calls it "a v0.1 release for development, testing, and experimentation"; its README scopes 1.0 to "Local development and continuous
integration (CI) test runs" and not "A multi-server deployment". Nothing in this corpus has run it.
Why that is tolerable here: the store is a projection; an engine that loses data costs the service its availability until a rebuild, and the record nothing. Under the archive's index
it is argued separately (ADR-0076 §4).
Substitution: any engine behind §5's interface, declared as ADR-0033 §2's rule has a deployment declare a substrate; one that is not open source meets §5 except S-6, and
says so.
A-1. The API is described once, in a model file; the GraphQL schema and the OpenAPI description are generated by a pinned tool, neither edited by hand.
A-2. The two interfaces are equal; a generated parity test fails the build when one offers what the other does not.
A-3. The API reads and never writes: no mutation, no method but GET and HEAD. Content enters by ingest (§9) and by no request.
A-4. Every response names its view and its revision digests (V-6); a cut view's or a digest's response is immutable, its entity tag the digest, cached without limit; latest
briefly.
A-5. The operations (table below), in both interfaces.
A-6. The interface is versioned, and a version only grows; a breaking change is a new version served beside the old.
A-7. Lists paged by cursor; a GraphQL query bounded in depth and cost, the bounds in the schema's description. This protects availability and nothing else.
A-8. Search is a second projection, built per view, immutable with a cut view, rebuilt from the store as the store is from the corpus (P-2).

text.tspan: §8 · Any reader may integrate, and none is privileged ⟨K7⟩

svg.text: U-1. The reference reader has no interface of its own. It uses §7 and nothing else (ADR-0073 §1 R-1). What it can show, any client can show.
U-2. Content is returned as a tree and not as markup: headings, paragraphs, lists, tables, code, figures, notes and binding references; a rendered HTML fragment is offered
beside it, and the tree is the contract.
U-3. The fields accessibility needs are mandatory in the tree: a figure's short alternative and long description, a table's header cells and caption, a heading's level, the
language of the unit and of any passage, an abbreviation's expansion on first use. Ingest refuses a unit that lacks one (ADR-0071 §8).
U-4. Marks and bindings are data, not decoration: a unit's status marks and each binding's node, clause, digest and freshness are fields.
U-5. A client may be a page, an application, a terminal or a program; cross-origin reads are allowed for the public units; an embeddable element is one such client (ADR-0073,
Options).
U-6. Who may read is the deployment's rule. The archetype's units are public under LICENSE-DOCS; a deployment's own may be restricted through its identity provider. A
restriction hides a unit and changes none.
§7 A-5 · The operations, whole, in both interfaces
List views; read a view's head
Kind, cut date, commit, manifest digest, counts
List a view's units, filtered by audience, domain and kind (ADR-0071 §2, §3, §6)
Unit heads with their state in that view
Read a unit in a view at a level
The content tree of MI, SI or DI, its marks, its bindings, its staleness
List a unit's revisions; read one by number, digest or time
Compare two revisions, or two views
From a node of the specification graph, list the units bound to it in a view
ADR-0071 §5's bindings, read backwards
Search a view
Units, with the level and passage matched
§9 · Ingest is the only way in; §10 · What the service does not hold; §11 · Degeneracy and the trusted base; §12 · Ratification condition, item by item
I-1. Ingest reads the corpus at one commit and writes revisions, bindings and, for latest, a manifest. A program in the repository, named by digest, that runs the same way by
hand and on a carrier (ADR-0069 §6 G-1).
I-2. Ingest refuses a name. It is given a commit, resolves it to a tree, and records the tree's digests. A cut is given the checkpoint's or the release's manifest and refuses a tree
that does not verify against it (ADR-0069 §1 P-1).
I-3. Ingest is idempotent. Run twice on one commit, it writes nothing the second time (S-4).
I-4. Ingest runs the gates of ADR-0071 §8 first, and writes nothing for a unit that fails one.
I-5. A carrier's merge is not a cut. Merging to the default branch moves latest; a checkpoint view is cut when the custodian cuts the checkpoint, and after bootstrap a
release view when a promotion's publication names it (ADR-0069 §8, §9 C-1).

text.tspan: §10 · What the service does not hold, and a deployment's own units

svg.text: H-1. No cognitive payload and no labelled item (ADR-0004; ADR-0047 §1). An example in a unit is written for it and is not taken from a round.
H-2. No secret and no deployment value in the archetype's units: "the deployment writes this".
H-3. A deployment's documentation is an overlay on the archetype's *(drafter's choice)*: keeps, replaces, adds or omits units by id, as ADR-0058 §1 (Proposed) has a
deployment's graph relate to the archetype's. A replaced unit names the archetype revision it replaces, so an upstream change shows as stale.

text.tspan: §11 · No degeneracy is declared, and no row is added

svg.text: No theorem takes a premise from the service. By ADR-0045 §2's test, its failure produces no admit, promotion or issuance. It can show a reader a wrong or missing page,
and ADR-0071 §11 says what bounds a reader who acts on one.
A deployment that serves its documentation some other way has made no declaration under ADR-0023 by doing so. It has only not met this record.
The service exists: ingest, store, both interfaces and search, with latest and at least two cut views
Not met: nothing is built
P-2 is seen: the store is dropped and rebuilt, and every revision and view digest is the same
§2 and §4 are seen: an overwrite refused at the store (S-4); a second, different write of a cut view refused (V-3); the contract tests
identical against latest and a cut view (V-1); a binding in a cut view returning the node's text at that cut after the node has
changed (V-2)
A-2's parity test exists and passes, and both descriptions are generated from one model with no hand edits
Annex A covers §7: every operation of A-5 is a row with a key condition, and no operation scans (S-2)
Not met: Annex A lists them, and nothing has run a
query
The engine of §6 is run under the service's load and a rebuild, and its build is pinned
Not met. Nothing in the corpus has run ExtendDB
A second client that is not the reference reader renders a unit from the API (U-1)

text.tspan: The store as the record: units authored through the service and kept only there

svg.text: Rejected (§1). It would be a system of record no record decided to keep, and its engine's maturity would then matter to the corpus

text.tspan: Git as the service: the carrier's API, tags as views

svg.text: Not taken. It keeps every revision and makes none equal: no levels, bindings, audience listing or search in a past tag. A carrier's tag also locates and does not identify (ADR-0069 §9 C-5)

text.tspan: A site generated per version, each a copy of the tree

svg.text: Not taken. Fits a few releases. Every checkpoint and every revision is not a few, and a copy per view shares nothing

text.tspan: A headless content system (Strapi, Directus, Payload)

svg.text: Not taken. Each gives REST and GraphQL over a relational store with editing through the service, which is the first row above
Not taken ⟨K6⟩

text.tspan: One interface written by hand and the other generated from it

svg.text: Not taken *(drafter's choice)*. The hand-written one becomes the real contract and the other drifts behind it

text.tspan: An interface generated from the store (a GraphQL or REST layer over the tables)

svg.text: Rejected. It would expose Annex A's keys as the contract, and §6's substitution with them
Not taken. Not asked for; the model of A-1 could generate it

text.tspan: A write interface for comments, edits or review

svg.text: Not taken (A-3). Review happens where the records' own review happens

text.tspan: History from the first cut after the service is built, with no backfill

svg.text: Open. V-7 backfills. This is cheaper and leaves G1 to G11 readable only through the carrier
Not taken. latest records each ingest's manifest, so any ingested commit can be read by time (L-3)

text.tspan: A search engine as a service (OpenSearch, Meilisearch)

svg.text: Open. A-8 fixes that each view has an index and is silent on what builds it. An index library embedded in the service is the drafter's recommendation

text.tspan: A link to a page in a checkpoint keeps working and keeps meaning the same thing.

svg.text: Old and new are served by one code path, so the old cannot rot unnoticed.
The store can be lost. A rebuild is a recomputation with a check, not a restore.
Two engines can stand behind one interface, and the choice of the first is cheap to reverse.

text.tspan: A deployment's reader, a terminal client and the reference reader are peers.
Everything is kept, so the store only grows.

svg.text: A search index per view multiplies with the number of cuts.
A single-table design fixes the access patterns in advance: Annex A must change before the API can.
The recommended engine is months old and declares itself unfit for production. The least proven part of this record.
Two interfaces are twice the surface to test, and A-2's parity is a standing cost.
Backfilled views (V-7) are thinner than cut ones, and a reader must be told so on every page.
The model language and generator of A-1, pinned: TypeSpec, Smithy, Protocol Buffers are candidates.
The canonical serialization of L-1, which must not change once a view is cut.
The service's language: Rust is the drafter's recommendation.
The search index of A-8, and ranking across three levels.
The backfill of V-7 for G1 to G11, or the custodian's decision not to.
The overlay of H-3, which leans on ADR-0058 (Proposed).
Names of people in units (an auditor's in a conformance report, ADR-0073 §7): personal data in an immutable revision. Not resolved.
Running ExtendDB under this design, and a second engine behind the same interface.

Annex A · The table's keys (reference design), whole. Drafter's choice throughout: the reference's design and not a requirement; §5 is the requirement. One table; n is a revision number zero-padded to eight digits; d is a SHA-256 in hex

text.tspan: ADR-0073 · The reference reader is React with Material UI over the public API alone (Context; §1 to §8)
Proposed · no marker on the drafter's reading · 2026.11.16, R1

svg.text: ADR-0072 serves the documentation to any client, and no client exists. The custodian asked for one built with React and Material UI, alternatives listed ⟨K8⟩, with five
properties ⟨K9⟩: responsive display, light and dark modes, a minimalist reading mode, assistive access, and WCAG compliance.
The five properties are not equally checkable. Reflow at a width, a contrast ratio and a missing text alternative can be computed. Whether a screen-reader user can find the
clause a runbook step rests on cannot. A program that reports no failures has shown that it found none of the failures it can find. The corpus's words: a mechanical gate
(ADR-0007), a check that "may refuse and never admit" (ADR-0069 §9 C-2), a field "checked or claimed" (ADR-0049).
Part of accessibility is not the reader's to supply: a text alternative, a heading's level, a table's header cells, the language of a passage belong to the content. ADR-0072 §8
makes those fields mandatory.

text.tspan: §1 · The reader is a client of the public API and nothing more ⟨K7⟩

svg.text: R-1. The reader calls only the API of ADR-0072 §7, with no credential a third party's reader could not hold. No route to the store, no endpoint of its own.
R-2. The reader holds no content. A page is a rendering of a unit's revision in a view, and its address names both. A link to a page in view G11 returns that page for as long as
the service runs.
R-3. The reader states nothing of its own. Its own text is navigation, labels and its accessibility statement (§7).
R-4. Every view is rendered by the same code path. Search, level switching, bindings and reading mode work in every view; the only difference a past view shows is a line
saying which view it is.
Both MIT-licensed; versions pinned by the lockfile, cited by digest when the reader is built (ADR-0069 §10.2).
M-1. A component is used as the library ships it only where it passes §6; otherwise wrapped or replaced, and the audit report names it *(drafter's choice: Material UI's WAI-ARIA
conformance is the library's claim, not a result this corpus holds)*.
M-2. The two colour schemes are one theme with two schemes, as CSS variables, set in the HTML the server sends.
M-3. Material Design's look is not a requirement. Density, elevation and motion defaults are turned down to what §5 and §6 allow.
RD-1. One document, one layout that reflows. No separate mobile site; no loss and no two-dimensional scrolling at 320 CSS pixels (WCAG 1.4.10); usable at 400% zoom.
RD-2. What cannot reflow scrolls inside its own region: a wide table, a code block, a diagram, each in a labelled, keyboard-focusable region.
RD-3. Orientation is not locked (1.3.4); a pointer target is at least 24 by 24 CSS pixels (2.5.8).
RD-4. Navigation collapses, and content does not. The unit's text, its level switch, its status marks and its bindings stay on the page.
LD-1. Two schemes, and the first visit follows the device (prefers-color-scheme); a reader's own choice overrides it, kept on that device, never part of a page's address.
LD-2. Both schemes meet the same contrast: 4.5 to 1 for text (1.4.3), 3 to 1 for controls and graphics (1.4.11); each scheme audited separately (§7).
LD-3. Nothing is said by colour alone (1.4.1): a status mark is a word; a stale binding is a word and an icon with a text alternative.
LD-4. A diagram has a rendering for each scheme, or draws in the text colour. The corpus's diagrams are generated, so the generators owe a second palette (Open
obligations).
LD-5. A user's forced colours (forced-colors) are respected.

text.tspan: §5 · Reading mode ⟨K9⟩: one unit, at one level, as a single column of text, with nothing else on the page

svg.text: RM-1. It is the page as the server sends it *(drafter's choice)*: complete HTML with its styles, readable, followable and printable with no script. Scripts add search, the level
switch without a load, and the scheme control.
RM-2. It has its own address.
RM-3. The column is at most 80 characters wide; size, line and paragraph spacing under the reader's control with no loss (1.4.12; 1.4.8 at AAA).
RM-4. Reading mode may hide navigation and never a mark or a binding. The view, the marks and the staleness stay at the head of the column; each binding becomes a
numbered note at the foot with its clause, module or policy and its digest. A mode that dropped "author-ratified" to look cleaner would make every page in it a publication
ADR-0029 §3 forbids.
RM-5. Print is reading mode on paper, each link's target and each binding's digest written out.
AA-1. Native elements first; ARIA only where HTML has no element for the pattern. Every control has a name, a role and a value a program can read (4.1.2).
AA-2. The page's structure is the unit's structure: heading levels, table headers, list nesting and reading order from the content tree ADR-0072 §8 returns (1.3.1, 1.3.2).
AA-3. Everything works from a keyboard (2.1.1), no trap (2.1.2), in reading order (2.4.3), a visible focus indicator (2.4.7) not covered by a fixed header (2.4.11); a skip link to
the unit's text (2.4.1).
AA-4. The level switch is three named controls, MI, SI and DI, each a link to an address. Nothing a reader needs appears only on hover (1.4.13).
AA-5. A change the reader did not ask for is announced: a route change moves focus to the new unit's heading; search results and a not-latest notice are status messages
AA-6. Motion is off where the device asks (prefers-reduced-motion), nothing flashes, nothing times out.
AA-7. Non-text content carries the text the unit supplies (1.1.1): a short alternative and a long description on the page. Where a unit supplies none, the reader shows "no
description supplied"; ADR-0071 §8 refuses that unit at release, so the words mark a defect in a view cut before the gate existed.
AA-8. Language is declared for the page (3.1.1) and for a passage (3.1.2); a glossary term links to narrative/glossary.md as the unit binds it.
AA-9. Help is in the same place on every page (3.2.6), and navigation keeps its order (3.2.3).

text.tspan: §8 · No degeneracy is declared, and no row is added

svg.text: No theorem takes a premise from a reader. A reader that fails shows a page wrongly or not at all; what a person then does is bounded as ADR-0071 §11 says: by the admit
path for a principal, by the rules floor for a key-holder. A reader that drops a status mark breaks RM-4 and ADR-0029 §3's rule, a defect in the reader and not a change in any
guarantee.
§7 · Conformance is to WCAG 2.2 at Level AA, and it is a dated audit ⟨K9⟩ (drafter's choice of version and level; the custodian said "WCAG Compliance"); §9 · Ratification condition, item by item

text.tspan: §7 · WC-1 to WC-6. WCAG 2.2 is the W3C Recommendation in force and is ISO/IEC 40500:2025; WCAG 3.0 is a Working Draft and is not a target

svg.text: WC-1. A release of the reader carries an accessibility conformance report: a dated results file, cited by digest, never edited after it is written (ADR-0069 §6 G-1). It names the reader's build by digest, the views and pages examined, both schemes, reading mode, each A and AA criterion with its result, and every
known failure. Not written.

WC-2. The report has two parts, and only the second supports a claim. *Computed*: pinned checkers over the pages examined; a clean run refuses nothing and establishes nothing; a failure refuses the release by the ratchet ADR-0069 §10.2 uses. *Examined*: a person's audit against each criterion, with a
keyboard alone and at least two screen readers on two platforms, named with versions; the person is named and says whether they wrote any of the reader.

WC-3. A release says *checked* or *claimed*. *Checked*: the examined part is complete for that build and was done by someone who did not write it. *Claimed*: anything less, and the accessibility statement uses that word.
WC-4. The claim covers the reader and the content of the views named, together. Content defects are reported against the unit (ADR-0071 §8), not waived as "content".
WC-5. Four AAA criteria are met in reading mode as advice: 1.4.6, 1.4.8, 3.1.3 (by the glossary links), 3.1.4. Marked *advice*, no part of the claim.
WC-6. Another reader makes its own claim. A deployment's or a third party's client inherits the content's fields and nothing of this reader's report.
The reader exists and serves every unit of ADR-0071 §3's set, in latest and in at least one checkpoint view, from the service of ADR-0072
Not met: nothing is built, and no unit is written
§1 is seen at the reference: the reader runs against the public API with no other access, and a second client that is not this reader renders the same unit from the same API
§3 to §6 are seen: reflow at 320 CSS pixels and at 400% zoom; both schemes at LD-2's ratios; reading mode read, followed and printed with scripts off; the keyboard path through a
unit, its three levels and its bindings
A conformance report under §7 WC-1 exists for a named build, its computed part reproducible from pins and its examined part by a person other than the author
Not met: no report, no auditor
The diagram generators emit a rendering for each scheme, and a long description for each diagram (LD-4, AA-7)

text.tspan: ADR-0071 and ADR-0072 are ratified, or this record is ratified with them

svg.text: Not met: both are Proposed
A reader who is not the drafter (ADR-0029 A2)
The custodian's reading of every drafter's choice, the WCAG version and level among them
Options considered, whole: the reader's framework and component library ⟨K8⟩ (one row is taken; licences as the drafter understands them, none checked); Other choices; Consequences; Open obligations
Taken ⟨K8⟩. A large component set with theming by CSS variables and two colour schemes. Its accessibility is the library's claim, which is why M-1 and §7 do not rest on it

text.tspan: React with React Aria or React Spectrum (Apache-2.0)

svg.text: Not taken ⟨K8⟩. Behaviour and accessibility without a visual design; the strongest record on assistive technology of the React libraries the drafter knows. The first replacement for any Material UI component that fails M-1
*(drafter's recommendation)*

text.tspan: React with Radix primitives or Base UI, styled in the repository

svg.text: Not taken. Unstyled, accessible primitives. More to build, and less to override

text.tspan: React with Chakra UI, Mantine, Ant Design, Fluent UI or Carbon

svg.text: Not taken. Comparable component sets. None was asked for, and none changes §3 to §7

text.tspan: A public-sector design system: GOV.UK Design System or USWDS

svg.text: Not taken. Each is built and audited for accessibility first, server-rendered HTML with little script, which is RM-1's shape. Neither is a React library, and each carries a government's look. Worth a second reading if the audits of
§7 go badly *(drafter's recommendation)*

text.tspan: Vue with Vuetify, Angular with Angular Material, Svelte or Solid

svg.text: Not taken ⟨K8⟩. Any of them can meet §1 and §3 to §7. Nothing in those sections is React's
Not taken as the reader. Kept as a way to meet ADR-0072 §8: a <topak-unit> element any page can host would be a second client, and would satisfy §9's second item

text.tspan: Server-rendered HTML with no client framework

svg.text: Not taken ⟨K8⟩. It is what RM-1 already requires of every page. A reader that was only this would meet §3 to §7 with the least code, and would lose search-as-you-type and the level switch without a load

text.tspan: A documentation generator: Docusaurus, MkDocs with Material, Sphinx, Antora, Astro Starlight,

svg.text: Not taken. Each builds a site from files at one commit. Versions are copies of the tree, which fits a few releases and does not fit ADR-0072 §2 and §4. None serves an API another client could use ⟨K7⟩

text.tspan: The carrier's rendering (Markdown on GitHub), as today

svg.text: Not taken. It is what exists. It has no levels, no bindings, no views, and its accessibility is the carrier's

text.tspan: WCAG 2.1 AA, which most regulation still names

svg.text: Not taken *(drafter's choice)*. 2.2 contains it, and adds focus not obscured, target size and consistent help
Not taken. The W3C does not recommend AAA as a general policy. WC-5 takes four criteria that suit reading
Rejected (WC-2). It would make a tool's silence an admit
Rejected. It changes what one reader's users get and nothing of the content, and it would be a third party's script on every page

text.tspan: A client-rendered application with no HTML until scripts run

svg.text: Rejected (RM-1). Reading mode would depend on the largest part of the reader working

text.tspan: The scheme in the address, so that a link carries light or dark

svg.text: Not taken (LD-1). The choice is the reader's, not the sender's

text.tspan: A dark scheme only, or a light one only

svg.text: Not taken ⟨K9⟩

text.tspan: A person reads the same unit, with the same marks, on a phone, a wide screen, paper or a screen reader.

svg.text: Conformance is a file with a date, a build and a name, and the word *claimed* is available for when it is not yet earned.
The reader can be replaced. It holds no content and no privilege.
Reading mode costs nothing extra, because it is the baseline the rest is added to.

text.tspan: Two schemes, reading mode and three levels multiply what an audit must examine.

svg.text: Material UI is a large dependency with its own design language, and M-1 expects to override parts.
A person's audit is slow and has to be repeated per release. Between audits a release is *claimed*.
Every diagram needs a second palette and a long description, and the corpus has many diagrams.
Server rendering is a running service, where a generated site would have been files.
The server-rendering framework for React. Not chosen.
The checkers of WC-2, pinned, and their ratchet.
An auditor who did not write the reader (WC-3).
A second palette and long descriptions from the diagram generators (LD-4, AA-7), which touches skills/generating-corpus-diagrams and diagrams/.
Mathematics and TLA+ in a page: a rendering a screen reader can speak. Not designed.
Whether EN 301 549 or Section 508 is also claimed. Not read for this draft.
Languages other than English. AA-8 declares language; no translation is planned.

text.tspan: History, whole: two rows for each record, and R1 is the same change three times

svg.text: Initial draft. User documentation is a derived layer that decides nothing and ranks below the narrative. Twenty-one readers are listed by position: holding a seat, at the gate or a trust root, and outside. The document set is listed for Build, Run, governance, external, every reader and the command-chain overlay, each row with its readers, the records it rests on

and what no record yet decides. Every unit is read at three levels, MI, SI and DI, mapped to C4's four; a level may leave out and never add, and a limit travels with its guarantee. A binding ties a statement to a node by digest, with a relation and a reader: every statement at DI, every must at SI, every guarantee or limit at MI. Status marks are ADR-0029 §3's.

A stale unit is served and marked, and only a reading clears it. A release is a manifest cut under seven mechanical gates that check form and not meaning. No degeneracy and no trusted-base row, because a reader is bounded by the admit path or by the rules floor
The custodian's request of 2026.11.16; the role and document inventory made for
this draft
Drafted 2026.11.16 by the assistant at the custodian's direction,
not reviewed
R1
Revision before ratification

Renumbered from ADR-0070 to ADR-0071, with its five siblings, each up by one: the set is now ADR-0071 to ADR-0076. ADR-0070 was already taken by a record in flight on another branch, which the first draft's check of branches missed because it looked only at the branches this clone had fetched. Every cross-reference among the six, every

degeneracy id and the index rows moved with the numbers. The old numbers are not shown struck at each place, since the change is the same at every one. The provenance note says which record holds ADR-0070 and that it was not read. No decision text changes
The custodian's question of 2026.11.16; git ls-remote, and pull request #51
Drafted 2026.11.16 by the assistant at the custodian's direction,
not reviewed

Initial draft. The documentation service is a projection of the corpus that can be dropped and rebuilt to the same digests, and is not a system of record. A unit's revision is immutable and addressed by digest, and every revision stays reachable. A unit is drafted, released, superseded or withdrawn, with withdrawal a revision and disposal not a state. A view is a

manifest; latest moves and every checkpoint and release view is cut once, and every operation is defined for every view. The store is one table with a composite key and secondary indexes, reached only through the DynamoDB interface; the reference's engine is ExtendDB on PostgreSQL, recommended with its immaturity stated. GraphQL and REST are

generated from one model, equal and read-only. Any reader may integrate and none is privileged; the fields accessibility needs are mandatory in the content tree. Ingest is the only write path and starts on a digest. No degeneracy and no trusted-base row. Annex A gives the keys
The custodian's request of 2026.11.16
Drafted 2026.11.16 by the assistant at the custodian's direction,
not reviewed
R1

Initial draft. The reference reader is a client of ADR-0072's public API with no privilege and no content of its own. It is React with Material UI, pinned. Pages arrive as complete HTML; the layout reflows from 320 CSS pixels; there is a light and a dark scheme following the device; reading mode is the scriptless page and never hides a status mark or a binding;

assistive access is stated as nine requirements. Conformance is to WCAG 2.2 AA, as a dated report with a computed part that may only refuse and an examined part by a person, and a release says *checked* or *claimed*. No degeneracy and no trusted-base row. Alternatives listed

What a reader should take from the three together. The layer (ADR-0071) says what is written and for whom, and that none of it decides; the service (ADR-0072) says how every revision and every cut view stays reachable and equal, from a store that can be thrown away; the reader (ADR-0073) says how a page shows a unit without adding to it, and that its accessibility is a claim until a named person has examined a named build. Every ratification condition of all three is not met, each ends with the custodian's reading of the drafter's
choices, and each depends on the one before it being ratified or ratified with it. G12 item 116 lists the set among what is owed.
